newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed a quiet session slightly lower and dealers said prices and yields looked set to remain close to current levels for the time being.
The next major market event is the July 1 and 2 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee to review U.S. interest rates.

Dealers said the majority market opinion was that inflation was not a threat to the U.S. economy and that the meeting would therefore not lead to another increase in U.S. interest rates on top of the 25 basis point rise implemented in March.
"Most people don't expect a rate hike and the whole thing will probably be a non-event for bonds," said one dealer.
Germany's ongoing attempts to meet the EMU budget deficit target of three percent of GDP were another theme foremost in trader's minds.
"If Germany is perceived to be making progress we could see yields come down at the long end, leading to some curve flattening," said one dealer.
"On the other hand if they don't seem to be getting anywhere then yield spreads versus Germany could move in the Netherlands' favour," he added.
The benchmark February 2007 Dutch government bond yielded a steady 14 basis points below the July 2007 bund on Monday.
Dealers said recent talk that institutions might be ready to allocate more cash to bonds, given the high levels to which share prices had risen, was beginning to fade again.
"To my mind shares look very expensive, but then you hear some brokers are revising their year-end forecasts for the AEX index up to levels of well over 900," said one.
The AEX, made up of 25 Dutch blue chip shares, closed 1.34 points lower at 860.86.
